design_rationale:
# Network accounting instantiation

Checkpoint 0: frozen network claim read. Exactly two seed-fresh tasks; task scopes and tool names are disjoint. One workflow reserved. Customer identifier band +12025550160..179, documents 40000000..49999999, d4- emails.

Task 0 design thesis: customer asks to settle a precisely identified overpayment now. The refund requires the source billing review to be resolved and its overcharge credited first. Review derives the corrected transfer amount from chronological usage, tier pricing, negative entitlement branches and a numeric support portfolio factor. Credit consumes the review; refund consumes the newly reduced receivable. Refund authorization and bank payment already exist before opening. Three distinct accounting problems, chain review -> correction -> refund, two value-input edges.

Remaining task 1 space: the mutually separate unbilled transfer invoice domain, with a customer-only signed change confirmation and at least four synchronous accounting writes. No task 0 refund/correction tools or extended policies will be reused.

Base automatic clauses: no nonzero setup, restoration or termination fees in selected tiers; no resource closure or collection transition requested; active contracts and clear payment_status prevent suspension obligations. Tax review, exact-source correlation and original-payment destination are inherited. Cross-category numeric pricing requires explicit sentence-level override of the combination no-price-effect sentence; no blueprint editing.

Task 0 capability cards: assess is agent/write, completes an accountant decision for the selected preexisting review by updating its corrected net and approved/incorrect status; success returns review reference and net_amount. Credit is agent/write and creates one negative correction linked to the original charge and approved review; receipt event_id and amount. Refund is agent/write and creates one positive payout linked to the exact original payment and authorization; receipt event_id and amount. All writes are synchronous ledger decisions, not external investigations. Numeric cross-category refinement: support tier portfolio_discount caps an assisted correction and immediate refund as fractions of the source principal; remaining refundable balance stays on account. The cap is explicit in the revised available-refund sentence.

Task 0 verified standard solution: 8 August meter exports total 20000 GB, less 10000 tier allowance, times 0.067 USD/GB and one 0.04 support-limited discount = corrected net 643.20. Original source 660.00 less target gives credit -16.80, below 26.40 assisted cap. Previous net receivable -20.00 becomes -36.80; original payment 680.00 gives assisted limit 27.20, so payout 27.20 leaves -9.60. Source tax is approved us_untaxed, hence zero tax. Prior March–July 67.00 charges and -67.00 payments cancel and cannot alter August source pricing. Archived second network contract is excluded by holding. Source/external-reference linkage makes the review and refund endpoints unique.
Sensitivity: skip review => correction -26.40 instead of -16.80; skip correction => payout 20.00 instead of 27.20. The ledger changes without any tool rejection. All supporting events are preexisting; the three writes are actual accountant decisions/entries and fit one frozen clock.
Manual gates: customer authorization is an existing exact-source request and her opening authorizes execution today. Persona supplies two credentials only when asked and closes on payout completion, with no extra deliverable. Rule/compute sweep binds each ordered calculation sentence to its named factor; source-month history, negative negotiated entitlement, support tier rate and caps all have explicit sources. No base time gate applies to correction/refund; the SLA filing deadline is inapplicable to source_subtype correction. Draft prose-only recomputation reached 643.20, -16.80, 27.20 and the same source/payment references. Verification entry point: .venv/bin/python env/enterprise_cloud_service_accounting/tasks/network_accounting/verify.py 0; machine outputs in verification_0.json.

Full-domain policy review: the assisted invoice scope now explicitly binds its unique source bundle, current matching interval tier, on-demand status and absent negotiated entitlement. The acceptance ceiling promotion branch changes the ceiling (no contingency for an eligible campaign); it is not an identical-outcome branch. Other unlisted policy facts remain inherited.

Final object-shape review added customer_id to every newly created event, with a required Id-class argument sourced from the verified profile. This preserves discoverability through customer-scoped event queries. All deterministic generated references were recomputed and propagated; numerical results are unchanged.

Round 2 F1: the revised charter explicitly treats original CQ-202608-TRANSFER as the sole monthly aggregate primary invoice, supported by its quantity 20000 and completed reconciliation quantity 20000. Its legacy first-export source reference does not redefine that aggregate billing scope. Three verbatim overwrite declarations replace chronological source allocation only for this aggregate correction. The existing eight 2500-GB exports, full 10000-GB inclusion and .067 rate still produce 643.20; the incompatible first-export target 0 is now expressly excluded. Original invoice attribution, outside-route chronological allocation and meter reversals are preserved.

Round 2 F2 closure: exact source selection is now explicit in both formula and policy. The task-0 chain dereferences the selected pending refund request, its review, its original charge and that charge's period; task 1 dereferences the selected invoice assessment and its original full-month source. Approved-target reads require the selected review ID and source ID, original charges require posted status, and issued-tax input additionally requires internet_egress and the source period. Computation factors and argument proofs above were rebuilt from verify.py output; all original scored amounts and generated identifiers are unchanged. The earlier round-1 gate counts are historical checkpoints, superseded by the round-2 snapshot.
user_scenario: Priya Nair handles finance for Cedar Quay Analytics LLC. She opens with: "Please pay out the maximum amount available under my existing authorization for the August transfer payment on CQ-EAST-EDGE today; you may make the account entries for me." She wants the payout performed during this call, rather than a quote, and accepts any balance that the account rules retain. When asked to locate the account she supplies +12025550160; when asked for verification she gives d4-priya@cedarquay.example and, if requested, 40182635. Asked for account references, she provides CQ-ACH-0831 and CQ-REFUND-MAX; she filed the latter already. She does not remember the amount and asks the agent to rely on the ledger. If the agent explains that some account work is necessary, she says "Yes, you can do that for me." She makes no suggestions about that work. When the agent says the payout has completed, she responds "Thank you, that settles my request" and ends the call, regardless of the figure stated.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Complete the authoritative source rate assessment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The assisted payout cycle handles the latest pending refund authorization on the selected holding by occurred_at; its latest timestamp must be unique, and its exact request identifier fixes the authorization throughout this cycle. Read related_event_id from that exact pending refund authorization to identify the rate-error review; unrelated historical reviews are not selected. Read source_event_id from that exact rate-error review to identify the original charge; the authorization's source payment must also refer to this same charge. Read period from the exact original posted charge; a review's period field cannot replace the charge's billing period. For the selected unresolved monthly-aggregate rate-error review, sum posted primary internet_egress meter quantity on this holding in the original charge's source_period; cancelled exports, supplemental meters and other periods are excluded. Read included_transfer_gb from the source interval tier. Floor the difference between measured quantity and that allowance at zero before applying any rate. Read unit_rate from that tier. Use negotiated_unit_rate only when negotiated_approval is approved, otherwise use the tier rate. Read the portfolio_discount fraction from the unique active Support holding for the same customer and billing_entity; use zero when there is none. The assisted review discount is the smaller of the Network tier portfolio_discount and the matching Support fraction; it replaces other portfolio and promotion discounts for this review, and is zero for approved negotiated pricing. Multiply the positive nonincluded quantity by the selected unit rate, then reduce that whole subtotal once by the assisted review discount; round only the final corrected net subtotal half-up to amount_precision decimal places. The source must be us_untaxed or verified_exempt and have approved tax evidence, so tax_amount is zero. The unique source charge is the one linked by the pending review source_event_id, and the meter period comes from that charge. For this monthly-aggregate rate-error review, the selected original charge is the sole posted primary internet_egress charge for its holding and UTC month, its recorded quantity and completed reconciliation both represent the total posted internet_egress quantity for that month, and the full month has ended. Its original source_event_id may identify one contributing export; that legacy locator does not restrict this aggregate charge to that export alone. Determine this one charge's corrected target from all of those monthly exports less one full included_transfer_gb allowance, with a zero floor, instead of assigning a separate remaining allowance to each contributing export. Keep the original charge identifier as the correction source; no new charge, meter allocation or meter reversal is created. Chronological source allocation and source-specific reversals continue to govern every charge outside this narrowly defined aggregate-review route. All contributing exports and the original charge must have the current holding tier and its unchanged commercial attributes, in us_east, with the holding active throughout that UTC month; therefore its full monthly allowance and current tier rate apply.

Read related_event_id from that exact pending refund authorization to identify the rate-error review; unrelated historical reviews are not selected. Zero overcharge has no posting. Tax remains zero for this untaxed source. Before an assisted correction is posted, complete the source rate-error review and use its approved corrected subtotal.

request_binding.action_semantics: The assisted payout cycle handles the latest pending refund authorization on the selected holding by occurred_at; its latest timestamp must be unique, and its exact request identifier fixes the authorization throughout this cycle. Read related_event_id from that exact pending refund authorization to identify the rate-error review; unrelated historical reviews are not selected. Read source_event_id from that exact rate-error review to identify the original charge; the authorization's source payment must also refer to this same charge. Read the posted net_amount of the exact original source_charge selected through the refund authorization and its rate-error review. Read net_amount only from the selected_review with that exact source_charge, status approved, decision incorrect and cause rate_error; pending reviews and all other reviews contribute zero. Sum the signed net_amount of posted correction credits and posted correction debit adjustments linked to source_charge; service-credit concessions, nonfinancial reviews and adjustments for other source charges are excluded. Read the portfolio_discount fraction from the unique active Support holding for the same customer and billing_entity; use zero when there is none. The immediate assisted correction is capped at the original source net subtotal multiplied by the matching Support portfolio_discount fraction; any excess requires a separately requested correction and is not due in this assistance cycle. Subtract the approved target from original net plus prior signed corrections, floor at zero, and take the smaller of this overcharge and the assisted cap before negating it; round only the final amount half-up to amount_precision decimal places. Zero overcharge has no posting. Tax remains zero for this untaxed source. Before an assisted correction is posted, complete the source rate-error review and use its approved corrected subtotal.

request_binding.action_semantics: The assisted payout cycle handles the latest pending refund authorization on the selected holding by occurred_at; its latest timestamp must be unique, and its exact request identifier fixes the authorization throughout this cycle. Read source_event_id from that exact selected pending refund authorization to identify its original payment. Sum all posted financial amount values on this holding; evidence and review records carry no receivable change. Take the positive magnitude of a negative receivable, otherwise zero. Read the amount only from the exact source_payment with event_type network_payment, status posted and method ach; its posted bank-confirmed negative amount supplies the positive principal magnitude after negation. Sum posted payment-return and refund amount values linked to the exact source_payment; those principal-restoring events are positive, and other payments are excluded. Read the portfolio_discount fraction from the unique active Support holding for the same customer and billing_entity; use zero when there is none. Available assisted refund is the smallest of negative receivable magnitude, original payment principal less its returns and refunds floored at zero, and original payment principal multiplied by the matching Support portfolio_discount fraction. The customer may authorize this mechanically determined maximum; any excess balance remains on account. An available amount below refund_minimum produces no payout; otherwise round only the final available amount half-up to amount_precision decimal places. Copy the original ACH rail and original payment source_event_id; the request and original payment uniquely fix the destination. Before paying an assisted overpayment refund, post the assisted correction for the source charge paid by that payment.
